explainerNotes.$comment: Existing explainer prose paragraph; no change planned.
explainerNotes.text: For 15% tip in your head: take 10% (move the decimal one place left), then add half of that. $45 bill → 10% is $4.50 → half is $2.25 → 15% is about $6.75. For 20%: take 10% and double it. These mental tricks are close enough for restaurant decisions; the calculator above will give you the exact number.

assumptions.text: Tip is calculated on the bill amount you enter.
assumptions.trimNote: Trimmed 2026-05-13. Original text was: 'Tip is calculated on the bill amount you enter. If you tip on the post-tax total, enter the post-tax bill.'. Trim rationale: triple overlap with assumption[3] (bill-as-entered, explicit) and faq Q2 (pre-vs-post tax). Length reduction with no informational loss.

assumptions.text: Per-person split is even; each person pays the same share of total.
Both decimal comma (18,5) and decimal point (18.5) are accepted.
The calculator uses the bill amount you enter. Enter the pre-tax subtotal if you want to tip before tax, or the after-tax total if you want tax included in the tip base.
assumptions.rationale: Explicit boundary against Sales Tax Calculator drift. Addresses 'restaurant calculator tax and tip' GSC intent (1 imp) without turning Tip into a tax-rate lookup tool.

methodology.rounding: Tip, total, and per-person amounts are calculated from the raw input values and displayed to 2 decimal places. Rounding is applied only when the result is shown.
methodology.roundingSource: reworded — consistent with Discount asset pattern. No algorithm claims (no 'banker's rounding', no 'half-away-from-zero').

limitations.text: Local tipping conventions are not looked up — defaults reflect US sit-down norms.
Automatic service charges (common for large parties or in some countries) are not detected; check the receipt before adding a tip on top.
This calculator does an even split. It does not handle itemized or uneven splits where people ordered different amounts.

limitations.rationale: Slightly longer, more explicit boundary. Prepares users for future /split-bill-calculator/ scope without naming it on-page.

faq.$comment: Single source of truth for both visible FAQ and FAQPage JSON-LD. Build pipeline generates JSON-LD from this array — never write a parallel faqSchema[] field.
faq.question: How do I calculate a 15% or 18% tip in my head?
answerParagraphs: For 15%: take 10% (move the decimal one place left), then add half of that. Bill of $40 → 10% is $4 → half is $2 → 15% is $6. For 18%: same trick, then add a bit more. For 20%: take 10% and double it.

faq.question: Should I tip on the pre-tax or post-tax total?
answerParagraphs: Pre-tax is the traditional standard in the US — you're tipping for service, not for tax. But many people tip on the post-tax total because it's what's printed on the receipt and it's easier. Both are common; the calculator works with whichever bill amount you enter.

faq.addressesQuery: tip calculator nyc, nyc tip calculator
faq.question: Is 20% standard in 2026?
answerParagraphs: For many US sit-down restaurants, including places like NYC, 18–22% is a common tip range. Use the percentage that matches your situation. Counter-service and takeout are more flexible — 10% or a few dollars is common, sometimes 0% if it's true counter-service.
faq.rewriteNote: Trimmed prior 'tip creep' explanation to compensate for NYC mention. Net length similar to original.

faq.addressesIntent: split-bill secondary use case (strategic, no GSC signal)
faq.previousQuestion: How do I split a bill unevenly?
faq.question: How do I split a bill with tip?
answerParagraphs: For an even split, use the formula per_person = (bill + tip) ÷ people. Example: $120 bill, 20% tip → tip is $24, total is $144, split 4 ways = $36 each. Enter your numbers in the calculator above for an instant per-person amount.

For uneven or itemized splits — when someone ordered more, or one person is paying a fixed share — ask the server to print separate checks (most US restaurants will), or calculate each person's share manually and add a flat tip percentage to each.
faq.rewriteNote: Question reframed from uneven-only to even-primary; even split formula + worked example added as paragraph 1; uneven boundary preserved as paragraph 2. No 'shared appetizer' content per W5 decision.
